text:
Kokoro TTS was evaluated as a Piper replacement in Sep 2026 and declined. The user judged Piper en_US-amy-medium good enough.

Numbers at the time, from the sherpa-onnx docs, measured on a Raspberry Pi 4:
- kokoro-en-v0_19 fp32: RTF 3.87 at 2 threads, 304 MB download.
- kokoro-int8-en-v0_19: 98 MB download. Exists as a GitHub release asset but is not listed in the docs, and has no published RTF.
- Piper medium voices: RTF ~0.48 at 2 threads, 64 MB.

RTF above 1 means slower than real time. Two things follow if anyone revisits this.

First, Kokoro is slow enough that PiperTtsManager.speak() would need reworking. It currently calls engine.generate() on the whole reply and only then plays it, so time-to-first-word grows with reply length. sherpa-onnx exposes OfflineTts.generateWithCallback(), which emits audio per sentence and would let playback start early. That rework interacts with the Bluetooth A2DP tail-wait logic in playAudio().

Second, Kokoro needs OfflineTtsKokoroModelConfig plus a voices.bin, not the VITS config Piper uses.

Matcha (matcha-icefall-en_US-ljspeech, 73 MB, RTF 0.56) was also declined: it lands between Piper and Kokoro on quality but costs the same code work as Kokoro. KittenTTS was declined for lack of any published quality or speed data.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
Upgrading the STT model was evaluated in Sep 2026 and declined. The user confirmed transcription accuracy is fine today, so the cost was not justified.

Why there is no cheap upgrade. An ONNX file is essentially just the weight tensors, so size is roughly parameter count times bytes per parameter. parakeet_tdt_ctc_110m is 110M parameters at fp32, which accounts for the whole 436 MB model.onnx. Accuracy tracks parameter count, so a better model is a bigger file. Quantization buys 4x once and is then spent.

The important point: parakeet_tdt_ctc_110m already sits at an unusually good accuracy-per-megabyte point, and the Parakeet family jumps straight from 110M to 0.6B with no middle rung. Everything checked that is genuinely more accurate is much bigger. Parakeet 0.6B int8 is 631 MB on disk, Whisper small.en is 606 MB and slower because it decodes autoregressively, SenseVoice is 999 MB. Whisper base and Moonshine base are smaller but weaker than what is already running.

Real delta for parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-int8: +195 MB in the APK and +390 MB on device, because every model is stored twice (see the storage note). The code change itself is small, about 15 lines in SpeechRecognizer.initialize(), swapping OfflineNemoEncDecCtcModelConfig for OfflineTransducerModelConfig with encoder/decoder/joiner files and modelType nemo_transducer.

One reason that would justify the switch: transducer models support hotwords and contextual biasing via OfflineRecognizerConfig, and CTC models do not. If specific names or jargon start getting mangled, that is the lever.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text:
Every model is stored twice on the device: once in the APK assets, once copied to filesDir by ModelAssets.ensureOnDisk. As of Sep 2026 that is about 876 MB for a ~438 MB asset set.

The copy exists because espeak-ng, used by Piper TTS, opens files by path and cannot read through AssetManager. STT has no such dependency, so sherpa-onnx OfflineRecognizer could take an AssetManager directly and skip the copy, saving roughly 436 MB.

This was considered in Sep 2026 and not done, because it is unmeasured. sherpa-onnx may read the asset into a heap buffer rather than memory-mapping it from disk, which would trade disk for RAM and be a downgrade on a 436 MB model. Anyone picking this up should measure before committing. It probably also needs noCompress for onnx in the Gradle config.

Separately: parakeet_tdt_ctc_110m ships as fp32. An int8 build would be about 110 MB instead of 436 MB for a small accuracy cost, but no prebuilt int8 of this exact model was found on Hugging Face or in the sherpa-onnx releases, so someone would have to run the ONNX Runtime quantizer and verify sherpa-onnx loads the result.
